title: CitationSet
description:
Field-level citations for one test case. Keys of `citations` are RFC 6901 JSON Pointers into result.json (e.g. `/policy_number`, `/coverage_list/0/coverage_insurance`). Each citation carries one or more `anchors`; an anchor is a renderable location in a source file. The UI draws every anchor of a citation as a yellow highlight.

COORDINATE CONTRACT for `page-region` anchors (the bounding-box case):
- `page` is 1-indexed and is the PDF page the highlight is drawn on. In the *-ocr.json artifacts that page is `ocr.words[].bbox.original_page`. `bbox.page` resets inside long OCR jobs (a 61-page policy comes back as pages 1–10 repeatedly) and must not be copied into `page` when it disagrees with `original_page`.
- `boxes[]` are axis-aligned rectangles expressed as FRACTIONS of the rendered page: `left`/`width` are fractions of page width, `top`/`height` are fractions of page height, origin is the TOP-LEFT corner, y grows downward. All four values are in [0, 1]; producers must clamp (a few OCR boxes in the fixtures overshoot by <1%).
- To render: x = left * pageWidthPx, y = top * pageHeightPx, w = width * pageWidthPx, h = height * pageHeightPx, where pageWidthPx/pageHeightPx are the on-screen size of the page as rendered (after any intrinsic /Rotate is applied by the viewer). This makes the schema independent of zoom and DPI.
- A citation that needs several visual pieces (a value wrapped across two lines, or a label plus its value) uses several `boxes` on one anchor, or several anchors. Do not emit one big union rectangle across unrelated text.
- `file` must be a PDF. For spreadsheets this is the `*-rendered.pdf`, never the .xlsx/.xls. Note: spreadsheet OCR block bboxes in this dataset are in CELL units (column/row indexes), not page fractions, and must not be copied into `page-region` boxes; use a `sheet-range` anchor instead.

citations.description: Map from JSON Pointer (into result.json) to the list of citations supporting that value. An empty array is a valid way to record 'searched, nothing found'.

jsonPointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. Array indexes are plain integers (`/coverage_list/0/coverage_name`).

Rect.description: Axis-aligned rectangle in normalized page coordinates (top-left origin, fractions of page width/height). See the coordinate contract on the root schema.

role.description: What this anchor highlights. `value`: the text that *is* the cited value. `label`: the field label that identifies it (e.g. `TENANT(S):` for the boolean field /Tenants, whose definition is 'label is followed by a non-empty string'). `context`: supporting text that does not contain the value verbatim (e.g. a header establishing which document this is). UIs may style these differently; `value` is the default yellow.

id.description: Stable identifier unique within the file; lets the UI accept/reject/edit a specific citation.

status.description: `proposed` = machine-generated and not yet reviewed. Reviewer actions move it to `accepted` or `rejected`. Rejected citations are kept (not deleted) so quality metrics can count them.

source.description: `auto` = produced by the citation run (deterministic or LLM). `manual` = drawn/entered by the reviewer in the UI.

method.description: Free-form producer tag for the auto path, e.g. `ocr-exact-match`, `ocr-fuzzy-match`, `llm:gpt-4.1-mini`, `reviewer`. Used to slice quality/cost metrics by strategy.

confidence.description: Producer's confidence that the anchors support the value. Omit for manual citations.

quote.description: Verbatim source text covered by the `value`-role anchors, as it appears in the source (before any normalization to the result format). If those anchors cover discontiguous segments, join the segments in reading order with a single space. A validator can check that the text under each anchor really is `quote`, and that `quote` is consistent with the result value under field-aware normalization (e.g. `$812.36` vs `812.36`, `Dec 20, 2025` vs `12/20/2025`; for boolean presence fields such as /Tenants, a non-empty `quote` is what supports `true`).

note.description: Short human-readable rationale, shown in the UI on hover.

anchors.description: All anchors are rendered together when this citation is selected. Mixed kinds are allowed (e.g. a `page-region` on the rendered PDF plus a `sheet-range` on the workbook for the same evidence).

PageRegionAnchor.description: One or more highlight rectangles on a single PDF page. This is THE bounding-box shape the UI renders.

file.description: File name inside the case `files/` folder. Must be the PDF that is actually rendered: `document-03.pdf`, or `document-09-rendered.pdf` for a spreadsheet.

page.description: 1-indexed PDF page. Equals `bbox.original_page` in the OCR artifact, not the resetting `bbox.page`.

boxes.description: Rectangles to fill yellow. Typically one per OCR line segment the evidence spans; producers merging adjacent OCR words into a single rect per line is encouraged.

provenance.description: Optional pointer back into the OCR artifact so the boxes can be re-derived or audited.

wordIndexes.description: Indexes into `ocr.words` for the words the boxes were built from.

TextSpanAnchor.description: A character range in a text-like source (txt, csv, eml, html, or a string field inside a JSON file). The UI highlights the range in a monospace text viewer.

pointer.description: Only for JSON files: pointer to the string field the offsets are relative to, e.g. `/bodyPlain` in an email-json file. When omitted, offsets are relative to the whole file's text content (UTF-8 decoded, line endings preserved).

start.description: 0-based inclusive offset in UTF-16 code units (JavaScript string indexing).

end.description: 0-based exclusive end offset. Must be > start.

JsonPointerAnchor.description: A whole value inside a JSON source file. Use when the value is an entire field (e.g. `/subject` of an email-json file); use `text-span` with `pointer` when only part of a string is the evidence.

SheetRangeAnchor.description: A cell or rectangular range in a spreadsheet (xlsx/xls/csv). This is the authoritative anchor for spreadsheet evidence. If the producer has also projected the range onto the `*-rendered.pdf`, add a sibling `page-region` anchor on the same citation; the UI uses whichever matches the active viewer.

sheet.description: Worksheet name. Required for xlsx/xls; omit for csv.

range.description: A1-style cell (`C7`) or range (`B4:D6`). Row/column indexes are 1-based as in Excel.
